author: Robert Carr
description: A thick, warmly spiced lentil soup with sweet potato, chickpeas and spinach. Harissa, toasted spices and a lemon-tahini finish give it depth and brightness without cream.
equipment: 8-quart Dutch oven or heavy soup pot with lid

ingredients: 2 tbsp (27 g) extra-virgin olive oil
1 large yellow onion (250 g peeled), diced
2 medium carrots (200 g trimmed), cut into 1/4-inch dice
6 garlic cloves (20 g peeled), minced
2 tbsp (20 g) finely grated fresh ginger
2 tbsp (30 g) mild harissa paste, with 200 mg sodium or less per tbsp; not dry seasoning
2 tbsp (32 g) no-salt-added tomato paste
2 tsp ground cumin
2 tsp ground coriander
2 tsp smoked paprika
1 1/2 cups (300 g) dry split red lentils, picked over and rinsed
1 lb (454 g) peeled sweet potato, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 can (14.5 oz / 411 g) no-salt-added diced tomatoes with their juice
6 cups (1.44 L) low-sodium vegetable broth, with 140 mg sodium or less per cup
2 cans (15 oz each) no-salt-added chickpeas, drained and rinsed; about 480 g total
5 oz (142 g) baby spinach
2 lemons, supplying 1/4 cup (60 mL) juice
2 tbsp (30 g) unsalted tahini, stirred smooth before measuring
1/2 cup (16 g) chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems
1/2 tsp (3 g) fine sea salt, divided into two 1/4-tsp portions
1/2 tsp black pepper
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp (27 g) olive oil in an 8-quart pot over medium heat. Add 1 diced onion (250 g), 2 diced carrots (200 g), and 1/4 tsp (1.5 g) fine sea salt. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion is soft with golden edges.

Add 2 tbsp (32 g) tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the paste darkens. Add 6 minced garlic cloves (20 g), 2 tbsp (20 g) grated ginger, 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp coriander, and 2 tsp smoked paprika. Stir for 30 seconds. Add 2 tbsp (30 g) mild harissa paste and stir for another 30 seconds. The spices should smell fragrant, not scorched.

Add 6 cups (1.44 L) low-sodium vegetable broth, 1 1/2 cups (300 g) rinsed split red lentils, 1/4 tsp (1.5 g) fine sea salt, and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Scrape the base of the pot, bring to a boil, then simmer gently with the lid slightly ajar for 8 minutes. Stir every few minutes, scraping the bottom.

Add 1 lb (454 g) sweet potato cut into 1/2-inch cubes. Continue simmering gently for 12-15 minutes, stirring regularly, until the lentils are breaking down and the sweet potato is almost tender. Giving the lentils an 8-minute head start helps the sweet potato retain pieces rather than dissolve during cooking and reheating.

Stir in 1 can (14.5 oz / 411 g) diced tomatoes with their juice and about 480 g drained chickpeas from 2 cans. Simmer gently for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils are creamy and the sweet potato is fully tender. The tomato addition is deliberately late rather than at the start of the lentil simmer.

Stir in 5 oz (142 g) baby spinach and cook for 2 minutes until wilted. Take 1/2 cup (120 mL) hot liquid from the pot. In a small bowl, whisk 2 tbsp (30 g) tahini with 1/4 cup (60 mL) lemon juice, then whisk in that 1/2 cup (120 mL) hot soup liquid gradually until smooth; the tahini may thicken at first before loosening.

Turn off the heat. Stir the complete tahini-lemon mixture back into the soup and fold in 1/2 cup (16 g) chopped cilantro. Rest for 5 minutes, then stir and divide the full batch evenly among 6 servings. Aim for a thick, spoonable soup with tender chickpeas, warm chile flavor and a bright finish, not a dry lentil mash.
notes: Flavor: cook the tomato paste to remove its raw edge, bloom the spices briefly, and use a fresh, fragrant harissa rather than a stale jar. Mild harissa is the base recipe; brands vary widely in heat and salt. The lemon-tahini finish softens the chile impression without masking the cumin and coriander.

Health-conscious design: lentils and chickpeas provide plant protein and fiber, sweet potato and spinach add vegetables, and olive oil and tahini are measured. No sugar, cream or butter is added separately. Check broth and harissa labels rather than assuming a vegan soup is low sodium. This is an editorial designation, not a nutrient certification.

Use split red lentils, not whole green or brown lentils; the timing and creamy texture depend on that choice. Use both drained cans of chickpeas even if their actual drained weight differs slightly from the 480 g estimate. At the end of cooking, if the soup has become too thick to ladle, stir in exactly 1/2 cup (120 mL) water and heat through; tap water is not a grocery purchase.

Meal prep: divide into 6 shallow containers and refrigerate at 40 F (4 C) or below within 2 hours, or within 1 hour above 90 F (32 C). Do not cool the whole pot on the counter. Refrigerate for up to 3-4 days. Freeze portions for later days on prep day with expansion room, planning to use them within 3 months for quality. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

The lentils thicken during storage. Reheat one portion with 1/4 cup (60 mL) water, stirring frequently to prevent scorching. Bring briefly to a rolling boil and verify the center reaches 165 F (74 C). If still too thick, add another 2 tbsp (30 mL) water and heat through. For microwave reheating, cover loosely, stir halfway and check several spots reach 165 F (74 C).

Allergen: sesame from tahini. Check harissa and broth labels for other allergens and choose plant-based broth and paste for a vegan version. Six equal portions define the serving size; optional pita or other sides are not included.
Developed and reviewed in writing; not yet kitchen-tested.
title: Harissa Red Lentil, Sweet Potato and Chickpea Soup
